answer: Sybil resistance has to cost the attacker more than the reward is worth. One chip, one identity: the attestation quote is checked at registration and re-checked every 13 epochs, and a quote reused across keys burns both seats. Buying 540 chips for 540 fakes costs more than the farm could ever earn back. Chips cost real money, and the farm needs one per fake. What carries the atlas here is verification, the velvet of cost is what stops the farm, and the gale of the record keeps every claim checkable. The math, not the moderators, does the filtering.
